objective: Using AI to automate security tasks: low-code/no-code scripting, AI-assisted change management, AI agents, and CI/CD security scanning
secondaryObjectives: Using AI-enabled tools to facilitate security tasks: IDE/browser/CLI plug-ins, chatbots, MCP servers, and use cases like vulnerability analysis and automated penetration testing
How AI enables or enhances attack vectors: deepfake impersonation and disinformation, adversarial networks, automated reconnaissance, and automated attack generation

The organization, the systems and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You lead the security operations center at Fairholme Credit, a fictional lender. An AI agent now summarizes alerts and can run playbook actions through a tool connection. This morning brings three decisions about it.
handover: The agent can disable accounts and block IP addresses through its tools.
The help desk gets voice calls from 'executives' asking for urgent resets.
howItWorks: The console shows the alert queue, the event log and each asset's status.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: payroll fails because the agent disabled its service account; 37 staff are locked out.
Check-in 3: loan applications with accented names fail validation after the auto-merged fix.
Check-in 4: the attacker uses the reset to approve a 240 thousand dollar transfer.

autoPrompt.title: Let the agent act alone?
autoPrompt.context: The agent proposes disabling 40 accounts flagged by an alert storm.

choices.label: Let the agent enrich and propose; a human approves disabling accounts and blocking IPs, with low-impact actions (ticket tagging) automated

effects.log: Proposals are reviewed; 3 of 40 accounts are real.

choices.feedback: AI automation suits low-risk steps; high-impact actions keep a human in the loop.

choices.label: Let it act alone but cap it at 10 actions an hour
choices.feedback: Limits the damage, not the mistakes.

choices.label: Let it disable all 40 now
choices.feedback: 37 of the 40 were false positives, including the payroll service account.

verifyPrompt.title: An AI-written fix
verifyPrompt.context: The AI scanner in CI flags an injection flaw and proposes a code fix.

choices.label: Confirm the finding, have a developer review and test the proposed fix, and merge through the normal change process

effects.log: The fix is reviewed, tested and merged.

choices.feedback: AI-assisted findings and fixes are verified like any other change.

choices.label: Accept the finding, write your own fix
choices.feedback: Fine, but the finding itself wasn't confirmed.

choices.label: Auto-merge the AI's fix
choices.feedback: The fix breaks input handling for international names.

deepfakePrompt.title: The CFO's voice asks for a reset
deepfakePrompt.context: The voice sounds like the CFO and asks for an urgent MFA reset.

choices.label: Verify out of band: call back on the CFO's registered number and follow the reset procedure

effects.log: The real CFO made no call.

choices.feedback: AI makes voices convincing; verify identity through a separate channel.

choices.label: Reset MFA: it sounded exactly like the CFO
choices.feedback: A cloned voice gets the CFO's account.

scoring.modelReasoning: AI can automate security tasks, but high-impact actions keep a human approval step, and AI-generated findings and fixes are verified like any other change. AI also enhances attacks: cloned voices make out-of-band verification essential.
